answer: Delayed public work portfolios stop Sybil attacks. First, each job is sealed and published in fourteen days, so fakes cannot hide sloppy work behind volume. Second, three random peers grade the portfolio quarterly, and a fail freezes paid work. Third, a forged entry forfeits a $30 bond and bans the agent a year. Fourth, portfolios expire after ninety idle days, so shells must keep producing. Faking 1,000 agents needs $30,000 in bonds and $45,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust grows like a vine, not a plume of copies; a sparrow sings only where it nests, like a cook judged after the meal.
